label: copy-phase input token j (fed-back j)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, on steps where the fed-back input token is j, i.e. the step right after the model output j. It never fires on j during the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other input token. Every activation falls under the predicate (recall 1.0). About 20% of copy-phase j inputs stay inactive, mostly when j was the first original token (input at recall_idx 1, right after <DEL>) or at the last copy step. Magnitude is largest when j sits at original positions 1-2 (input at recall_idx 2-3, e.g. c [j] y ...). It is weak when j is the first original token, and the second j in a jj run gets a lower value (about 0.55-0.77 of the first).

issues: Core claims hold. Activation is zero in the original and delimiter phases, every activation has in_tok == j, and recall is 1.0 on dev and test. Test scores match the report: P 0.800, R 1.0, F1 0.889, mass recall 1.0.

One part of the explanation is inaccurate: the claim that inactive j inputs come mostly from the last copy step. With to_go == 0, j inputs have precision 0.81 (dev), which is the same as the 0.80 base rate, so the last step is not an over-represented failure case. Only recall_idx == 1 (j was the first original token) is systematically weak, at precision 0.45. It accounts for about half of the roughly 18k false positives on dev.

After adding recall_idx >= 2, the remaining false positives (precision about 0.88-0.90) show no clear pattern. Precision ranged only 0.82-0.99 across output token as digit, vowel or j, first_tok == j, n_digits >= 2, recall_idx 2, 3 or >= 5, L >= 7, in_count >= 2 and prev_tok == j. The weakest slice is recall_idx >= 5 at 0.82, a mild decline at later positions, not a clean counterexample class.
The magnitude claims are consistent with the profile. Mass share peaks at recall_idx 2-3 (0.27 and 0.25) and is low at recall_idx 1 (0.065).
On test, adding recall_idx >= 2 gives P 0.877, R 0.895, F1 0.886, effectively tied with the simpler predicate (0.889). Keeping the simpler predicate is justified.
